channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Ministro de Lula vê eleições “mais fáceis que 2022”
item.description: Social Development Minister Wellington Dias said the Lula government needs to improve the communication of its third-term achievements, but expressed optimism about the 2026 elections, stating the political landscape is likely to be less complex than in 2022, despite ongoing challenges.

item.title: Lula exalta acordo UE-Mercosul, mas critica 'afirmativas falsas' sobre agricultura brasileira e barreiras ao biocombustível do país
item.description: President Lula praised the EU-Mercosul agreement, set to take partial effect on May 1, emphasizing its potential to create jobs, attract investment, and strengthen supply chains. He criticized what he called 'false claims' about the sustainability of Brazilian agriculture and barriers to national biofuels, urging Europeans to consider Brazil's clean energy matrix. The speech was delivered at the opening of Hannover Messe, where Brazil is the featured country, and included criticism of the Iran war, Trump's foreign policy, and the paralysis of the WTO.

item.title: Lula volta a mandar recados a Trump em discurso na Alemanha e diz que mundo “não pode se curvar” a quem faz guerra pelo Twitter
item.description: Lula criticized Trump during his speech at the Hannover Fair in Germany, stating that the world 'cannot bend' to a president who uses Twitter or email to impose sanctions and start wars. He highlighted the contrast between global war spending ($2.7 trillion) and lack of investment to end hunger, while questioning the effectiveness of the UN Security Council amid conflicts involving the U.S., Russia, China, France, and the UK.

item.title: Brasil, México e Espanha anunciam ajuda a Cuba
item.description: Brazil, Mexico, and Spain announced coordinated humanitarian aid to Cuba, expressing deep concern over the island's humanitarian crisis and urging respect for international law and territorial integrity. They called for a sincere and respectful dialogue with the United States, reaffirming their commitment to democracy, human rights, and multilateralism, while Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel stated Cuba does not seek war but reserves the right to defend itself against potential U.S. military intervention.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil é um dos menos afetados pela guerra no Irã
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil is among the countries least affected by the Iran war, citing its diversified energy matrix and emergency government measures, including the zeroing of PIS/Cofins on diesel and a R$ 0.32 per liter subsidy. He emphasized that Brazil does not face oil price spikes like many nations, as it exports only 30% of its fuels. Lula also criticized protectionism and advocated for multilateralism as a path toward fairer international cooperation.

item.title: O otimismo do relator do PL da Dosimetria sobre a derrubada do veto de Lula
item.description: Senator Esperidião Amin (PP-SC), rapporteur of the Dosimetry Bill, expressed confidence that President Lula’s veto will be overturned by the Senate on May 30, with minimal resistance expected outside the government’s allied base. He also sees an opportunity to revive discussions on amnesty for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, linking the current political climate to the Banco Master scandal investigations and criticizing the Supreme Court’s inquiry as arbitrary and undemocratic.

item.title: PT do Rio oficializa apoio a Paes e lança Benedita ao Senado
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro Workers' Party (PT) officially endorsed Eduardo Paes (PSD) as its gubernatorial pre-candidate and nominated Benedita da Silva for the Senate. The party described Paes' candidacy as the 'main electoral base' for Lula's 2026 re-election and advocated for direct elections as the most democratic option, following the interim appointment of Governor Ricardo Couto after Claudio Castro's resignation.

item.title: Caiado diz que Kassab "seria perfeito" como vice no interior de SP
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado said Gilberto Kassab would be the "perfect" running mate for the PSD presidential ticket, calling him the "greatest articulator" and noting his support is already secured. Caiado also criticized PT governments, linking them to corruption and factionalism, and made a veiled critique of Jair Bolsonaro by referencing his 2018 slogan "less Brasília and more Brazil," saying nothing changed. He emphasized security as a top priority, stating 60 million Brazilians are hostages of organized crime.

item.title: Lula chega à Alemanha para assinar parcerias comerciais e de inovação
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva arrived in Germany to sign 10 agreements in areas including defense, climate change, infrastructure, artificial intelligence, and bioeconomy, aiming to promote Brazil's reindustrialization and attract investment. His agenda includes a meeting with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, participation in the opening of Hannover Messe—the world's largest industrial fair, which honors Brazil this year—and the Brazil–Germany Economic Meeting. The initiative reflects Brazil's strategy to revive its industrial policy and position the country as a hub for innovation and business.

item.title: Lula desembarca na Alemanha para a Hannover Messe 2026, a maior feira industrial do mundo, e se reúne com Merz
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva arrived in Hannover, Germany, to attend Hannover Messe 2026, the world's largest industrial fair, where Brazil is the partner country. He held a private meeting with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, followed by a joint delegation talk, the fair's opening ceremony, and a dinner with business leaders. Promoted by ApexBrasil, the visit aims to strengthen strategic partnerships in defense, infrastructure, energy transition, bioeconomy, and AI, while positioning Brazil as an investment destination and addressing global issues like democracy, inequality, and climate change.

item.title: O mediador das conversas entre Flávio Bolsonaro e André Mendonça
item.description: TCU Minister Jorge Oliveira has served as the main liaison between Flávio Bolsonaro and STF Minister André Mendonça, who leads investigations into the Banco Master scheme and improper INSS discounts. Although Mendonça prefers to avoid electorally sensitive rulings, he ordered the arrest of the former BRB president in Operation Compliance Zero, indicating he cannot halt investigations. Oliveira, future TCU president, was a minister in Jair Bolsonaro’s government and has long-standing ties to the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Lula precisa “afinar a orquestra” para se reeleger, diz ministro
item.description: Wellington Dias, political coordinator of Lula’s campaign, says the president must 'fine-tune the orchestra' to win re-election in 2026 by improving communication and alignment among PT leaders. He views the election as easier than in 2022 and outlines strategies to attack Flávio Bolsonaro’s inexperience, maintaining polarization between 'humane' and 'inhumane' projects.

item.title: Lula chega à Alemanha para encontro com Friedrich Merz
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva arrived in Germany for a series of bilateral meetings, including a private meeting with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, participation in Hannover Messe, and discussions on artificial intelligence, climate, defense, and energy. The visit includes engagements with business leaders, German officials, and a tour of Volkswagen’s headquarters in Wolfsburg, before proceeding to Portugal.

item.title: Neurocientista conta como ‘desacelerou’ Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Neuroscientist Ricardo Caiado treated Jair Bolsonaro in the Papudinha prison using neuromodulation to improve sleep, reduce anxiety, and control hiccup episodes. After detecting autonomic nervous system imbalance — sympathetic overdrive and parasympathetic underactivity — the treatment, combined with breathing exercises, physical activity, and dietary changes, restored autonomic balance. The shift to house arrest was crucial, offering family support and a better environment for therapy.

item.title: Nó político em Minas pode empurrar Lula e Aécio para a mesma aliança; PT resiste
item.description: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB) is considering running for governor of Minas Gerais under pressure from Lula, with the possibility of an alliance between the PT and PSDB led by Aécio Neves. The PT leadership resists, calling the idea 'absurd', but acknowledges the need for Pacheco's electoral base in the country's second-largest voter college. Aécio Neves does not rule out forming a ticket with Pacheco for the Senate, despite refusing to appear at events with Lula, citing a historically positive relationship during Lula's early terms.

item.title: Entenda 4 pontos-chave do depoimento de Lincoln Gakyia que levou à troca do comando da PM-SP
item.description: The confidential testimony of prosecutor Lincoln Gakiya revealed alleged negligence by former PM-SP commander Colonel José Augusto Coutinho regarding bribery payments from the PCC to Rota police officers, which, combined with a request from prosecutor Bruno Servello Ribeiro, led to his replacement by Colonel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli. Coutinho’s defense denies having access to the inquiry and claims he was never informed of subordinates’ ties to organized crime. The São Paulo government states the change was due to Coutinho’s personal request and emphasizes technical criteria in military police personnel decisions.

item.title: Lula e Janja visitam a Basílica da Sagrada Família em Barcelona
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and First Lady Janja visited the Basilica of the Sagrada Família in Barcelona during an official trip to Spain, Germany, and Portugal, concluding Lula’s European agenda. He described the visit as a 'moment of peace, prayer, and reflection,' emphasizing dialogue as essential to address global challenges. The agenda included meetings with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, participation in the Brazil–Spain Summit, the Democracy Defense Forum, and the Global Progressive Mobilization, focusing on economic cooperation, democracy, and countering the rise of the right.

item.title: Lula é recebido por chanceler alemão em Hannover
item.description: President Lula was received by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Hannover, Germany, with military honors at Herrenhausen Palace. The agenda includes the opening of the Hannover Industrial Fair, the world's largest in its sector, and a dinner with business leaders.

item.title: Passagem de Lula pela Alemanha inclui reunião com o chanceler Friedrich Merz
item.description: President Lula visited Germany on April 19, 2026, for a bilateral agenda that included a meeting with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, participation in the opening of the Hannover Industrial Fair — where Brazil was honored with a 2,700 m² exhibit focused on renewable energy and technology — and the launch of the third round of high-level intergovernmental consultations between Brazil and Germany, with expectations to sign at least ten agreements on defense, environment, bioeconomy, infrastructure, and AI.

item.title: PT avalia incluir estatal de minerais críticos no programa de governo
item.description: The PT is evaluating the inclusion of Terrabras, a state-owned enterprise for rare earth and critical minerals, in Lula’s 2026 government program to strengthen sovereignty over strategic resources. The proposal is under internal and congressional debate, with two bills (PL 1733 and PL 1754) introduced, the latter facing resistance over claims of unconstitutionality.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que aumenta fiscalização de clubes formadores
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.387/2026, requiring youth athlete training clubs to register their programs with municipal councils for the Rights of Children and Adolescents, strengthening oversight to prevent abusive practices in training centers. The measure, originating from Bill 1.476/2022 by former deputy Milton Coelho, was approved by the Senate with a favorable report from Senator Jorge Kajuru, who emphasized the need to safeguard the physical, emotional, and moral integrity of young athletes.

item.title: INSS tira mais votos de Lula do que Master
item.description: The article argues that, despite the media focus on the Banco Master scandal, the embezzlement of billions from the INSS has a significantly greater electoral and social impact, costing Lula more votes than the Banco Master case itself. It contends that the public underestimates how corruption in social security erodes trust in the government.

item.title: Palanques, alianças e aval do pai: o que pesa na definição de quem será vice de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is expected to choose his running mate by mid-2026, prioritizing political alignment and personal trust, with two main scenarios: a candidate from the União-Progressistas federation (notably PP) or Romeu Zema (Novo). Both face challenges: Novo lacks national reach and Zema’s approval is declining in Minas Gerais, where his ally Matheus Simões left the party to join PSD and support Ronaldo Caiado, creating tension with Bolsonarists due to the rupture with Gilberto Kassab and the PSD.

item.title: Investigação sobre corrupção na política do Rio avança na PF
item.description: The Federal Police is in an advanced stage of investigation into bribery payments to Rio de Janeiro state legislators linked to organized crime, including the illegal gambling game 'jogo do bicho' and e-cigarette smuggling mafia. Minister Gilmar Mendes confirmed the investigation during a recent STF ruling, stating that 32 or 34 ALERJ deputies receive illegal monthly payments. The probe is connected to the state succession following Governor Cláudio Castro’s resignation.

item.title: Coordenador da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro defende redução do poder do Congresso sobre o Orçamento
item.description: The coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), has been advocating in private conversations for reducing Congress's power over the Budget, proposing that the share of parliamentary amendments be decreased so the Executive can regain control over these resources. The measure is presented as a strategy to strengthen governmental management in case of victory in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Os gastos de Lula com viagens internacionais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is nearing R$1 billion in international travel expenses since 2023, according to O Globo. So far, spending totals R$972 million abroad and R$6.2 billion domestically. His current agenda includes visits to Spain and Germany.

item.title: Conversas do Master confirmam que o celular é o maior delator do Brasil
item.description: Investigations into the Bolsonarist coup attempt revealed that the cell phones of those involved were the most decisive evidence, surpassing even plea bargains. Now, in the inquiry into alleged irregularities at Banco Master, led by Daniel Vorcaro, authorities again expect the suspects' cell phones to provide the most reliable evidence. The cell phone, therefore, remains Brazil's greatest informant, due to its ability to record conversations, locations, and digital transactions.

item.title: Governo Lula já gastou quase R$ 1 bilhão com viagens internacionais
item.description: The Lula government has spent nearly R$1 billion on international travel since 2023, with the president currently on a new tour of Spain, Germany, and Portugal. The total includes expenses for flights, accommodation, security, and diplomatic staff, according to an exclusive report. Full access to the article requires a subscription to the publishing outlet.

item.title: Datafolha: 67% dos brasileiros têm dívidas financeiras e 21% parcelas em atraso
item.description: A Datafolha survey shows 67% of Brazilians have financial debts and 21% have overdue installments, reflecting a household income commitment of 29.3% in January — a historical high. Heavy reliance on credit card revolving debt (used by 27%), perceived as creating 'snowball' debt by 84%, contributes to Lula’s electoral challenges despite controlled inflation and policies like income tax exemption up to R$5,000. In response, 64% cut leisure spending, 60% reduced eating out, and 52% bought less food.

item.title: Lula desembarca na Alemanha em busca de negócios e parcerias em tecnologia
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva arrived in Germany to attend Hannover Messe 2026, where Brazil is a partner country, aiming to sign around ten agreements in technology, defense, AI, energy, and climate. His agenda includes meetings with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, the opening of the industrial fair, participation in the Brazil–Germany Economic Meeting, and the 3rd High-Level Intergovernmental Consultations. The visit strengthens Brazil’s strategic partnership with Germany, its fourth-largest trading partner, with US$20.9 billion in trade in 2025.

item.title: Apoiadores de Lula tentam alavancar pré-campanha com jingles
item.description: Supporters of Lula are producing jingles and videos in popular rhythms such as samba, forró, and sertanejo to boost his pre-campaign amid declining poll numbers. The content highlights his life story, from humble beginnings to social programs like Bolsa Família and Minha Casa, Minha Vida, and references his imprisonment during Operation Lava Jato. A YouTube channel, 'Som do Brasil com Lula', has surpassed 1.1 million views with at least 30 such videos.

item.title: Como o PT conseguiu emplacar um militante no hoje estratégico cargo de ministro do TCU
item.description: The PT succeeded in appointing deputy Odair Cunha (PT-MG) to the TCU via a secret vote in the Chamber, marking a strategic victory after previous defeats of José Pimentel and Paulo Delgado. His appointment comes at a time of balance in the tribunal, with four ministers aligned with Bolsonarism and four independents, and could influence key decisions, such as the case of Miriam Belchior, who was spared condemnation over fiscal pedalings. The party emphasizes Cunha’s independence and support for parliamentary amendments, signaling that the conflict between Congress and the STF over public fund usage remains unresolved.

item.title: Empresa de Marçal repassou R$ 4,4 mi a Mc Ryan, diz PF
item.description: The Federal Police reported that a company linked to Pablo Marçal (Union Brazil), former São Paulo mayoral candidate, transferred R$4.4 million to musician MC Ryan, who is accused of leading a money laundering scheme for the PCC. The transaction is under investigation as part of an operation targeting organized crime.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro apoia fim da reeleição, mas nem um terço dos brasileiros acha que isso aumenta sua chance
item.description: In March, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro introduced a PEC in the Senate to end re-election for presidents, governors, and mayors. However, a Genial/Quaest poll conducted between April 9 and 13 with 2,004 respondents found that less than one-third of Brazilians believe this proposal would improve his electoral chances. While aligned with a rhetoric of political renewal, the measure does not appear to significantly influence public perception of his viability in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Nova lei amplia acesso a terapias e vacinas contra o câncer no SUS
item.description: Law No. 15.385/2026 establishes the National Policy for Cancer Prevention and Control within the SUS and the National Patient Navigation Program for Cancer Diagnosis, expanding access to advanced therapies, vaccines, and diagnostic tests. Signed by President Lula and Health Minister Alexandre Padilha, the law aims to reduce import dependence, stimulate national production, public-private partnerships, and the use of AI and genetic sequencing in cancer care.

item.title: Mourão recebe Messias e diz manter voto contra indicação ao STF
item.description: Senator Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS) met with Jorge Messias, the Attorney General nominated by Lula for the Supreme Federal Court, and stated he will maintain his vote against the nomination. Mourão said the meeting was held at the request of various individuals, but it did not change his position.

item.title: Mulheres viram foco central das campanhas de Lula e Flávio
item.description: The 2026 campaigns of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are focused on winning over female voters, whom both candidates struggle to gain approval from. Lula is leveraging initiatives led by First Lady Janja, such as the National Pact Against Femicide and speeches on gender-based violence, while Flávio seeks to reposition himself amid similar challenges. With women making up 52.8% of the electorate, this demographic has become pivotal in the presidential race.

item.title: Governo prepara decreto para tentar frear aumento da violência digital contra as mulheres
item.description: The Ministry of Justice is preparing a decree to be signed by Lula within 30 days to combat the rise in digital violence against women. The initiative includes a series of measures to address this growing problem. The full article is available only to subscribers after registration.

item.title: 'Enquanto o PT estiver nos ajudando, o Flávio vai continuar jogando parado'
item.description: A member of Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign stated that he will remain inactive as long as the PT helps his candidacy, suggesting a deliberate strategy of passivity. The remark indicates the campaign is counting on indirect PT support to avoid direct confrontation and keep Flávio in a favorable position without active effort. The content is exclusive to subscribers and requires registration for full access.

item.title: PSDB traça meta de quase triplicar bancada na Câmara
item.description: Under Aécio Neves’ leadership, the PSDB aims to nearly triple its Chamber of Deputies caucus from 13 to about 35 seats in the 2026 elections. The party is also advancing strategic candidacies: Paulo Serra for governor of São Paulo and Ciro Gomes for president, following a meeting with Aécio.

item.title: Estratégias de Lula e Flávio contra adversário miram Master, 6x1 e dívidas
item.description: President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro are intensifying their campaign strategies against their respective rivals, focusing on issues such as debt, corruption allegations, and narratives like '6x1' and 'Master' to undermine their opponents' image. Both seek to link their rivals to financial scandals and questionable practices, while reinforcing their own electoral bases with discourses of order and justice.

item.title: Terrabras, ministério e estatal devem entrar em plano de Lula 4
item.description: The PT is drafting Lula's government plan for a potential fourth term, including three structural proposals: the creation of the state-owned Terrabras, the recreation of the Ministry of Public Security, and the launch of a new state-owned fuel distributor. These initiatives are deemed unfeasible before the end of the current term but may be included in the government program as internal party commitments, without requiring immediate legislative approval. The proposal for a new fuel distributor aims to circumvent the non-compete clause from the sale of BR Distribuidora (now Vibra Energia), though experts warn the contract remains legally valid and could trigger litigation.

item.title: Programa de Lula para reformas fracassa e empresta 3% do esperado
item.description: Lula's Reforma Casa Brasil program, launched in October 2025, has severely underperformed, disbursing only R$1.017 billion (3.4% of the expected R$30 billion) in five months, with 63,111 loans issued. Low demand led to interest rate cuts and income bracket revisions, while rising default rates raise concerns, as the government would bear losses through the Social Fund and Popular Housing Guarantee Fund. The program's failure undermines Lula's hopes to boost his approval ahead of the October 2026 elections, particularly given the Northeast—his traditional stronghold—accounting for 33.6% of beneficiaries.

item.title: Desconfiança no STF atinge patamar recorde e ultrapassa 50% pela primeira vez, aponta Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows that, for the first time, over half of Brazilians (53%) distrust the Supreme Federal Court (STF), while only 41% express confidence — a historic low since 2022. This decline is tied to the Banco Master scandal and allegations of judicial involvement with banker Daniel Vorcaro, with trust and distrust crossing between August 2025 and March 2026. Distrust is highest in the South (62%) and Southeast (59%), and rises with income: 60% of those earning above five minimum wages do not trust the STF.

item.title: Lula tratará Flávio como submisso a Trump; senador atacará fraqueza petista na economia e segurança
item.description: Lula plans to attack Flávio Bolsonaro by portraying him as subservient to Donald Trump’s interests and a threat to Brazilian sovereignty, using rhetoric of treason following U.S. sanctions and tariffs. Flávio counters by criticizing Lula’s government for weakness in the economy, public security, and anti-corruption efforts, seeking to capitalize on his rise in second-round polls, where he is now technically tied with the president. Both candidates have defined their core campaign strategies: Lula emphasizing external threats and Flávio highlighting internal failures of the PT administration.

item.title: Tarcísio trocou chefe da PM após acusação de omissão em caso de corrupção de policiais pelo PCC
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas dismissed Colonel José Augusto Coutinho, commander of São Paulo's Military Police, following allegations of omission regarding police involvement with the PCC, including bribery and leaks of classified information. The move was influenced by confidential testimony from prosecutor Lincoln Gakiya and a request from military prosecutor Bruno Servello Ribeiro to investigate Coutinho’s conduct. He was replaced by Colonel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli, the first woman to lead the force in 200 years.

item.title: Desconfiança no STF atinge patamar recorde e ultrapassa 50% pela primeira vez na pesquisa Quaest
item.description: For the first time in the historical series of the Genial/Quaest poll, initiated in 2022, more than half of Brazilians (53%) distrust the Supreme Federal Court (STF), while only 41% express confidence. This erosion of credibility is directly tied to the Banco Master scandal and revelations of judges' involvement with banker Daniel Vorcaro, with the steepest decline occurring between August 2025 and March 2026. Rejection is highest in the South (62%) and Southeast (59%), and rises with income: 60% of those earning above five minimum wages distrust the STF.

item.title: Caiado procura Ciro Gomes
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD pre-candidate for presidency, approached Ciro Gomes in early April to ask if he would run for president. Ciro said he is focused on running for governor of Ceará. Caiado made the approach before the PSDB formally invited Ciro to run for president on April 14.

item.title: Como a guerra chega na eleição
item.description: The war against Iran is directly impacting Brazil, particularly through rising fuel prices, affecting public economic perception despite positive official indicators. According to the Genial/Quaest poll, 84% of Brazilians feel affected by fuel price increases, with 38% blaming the international war and 25% attributing it to the Lula government’s economic decisions. The anticipated end of the conflict on Friday is seen as positive news for the Brazilian government, but the gap between perception and reality continues to distort the electoral landscape.

item.title: Os Supremos
item.description: The article argues that authoritarian governments, regardless of ideology, seek to control the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to maintain the appearance of democracy while undermining its checks and balances. In Brazil, the STF is seen as the final arbiter of right and wrong, making it a target for governments aiming to erode its legitimacy—such as Bolsonaro’s administration, which attacked its justices to facilitate a potential coup. The piece is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.
